answer: A decentralized agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, slashable stake and require that stake to back costly actions, such as posting a bid or attesting to a task. If several agents collude to fake reputation, auditors can challenge their claims against task evidence; proven fraud burns the backing stake and removes earned reputation. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence without multiplying capital, so a sybil campaign must lock up more funds and risks losing them. The vine of trust may climb a ridge, but a glacier of fabricated accounts still has to pay.
